Does a simple Kotlin project with a single `@Produces` bean that is mocked work properly?

Yes, if bean is not used anywhere else - it works. Example:
https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L24
So, [here](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L19) we have mocked bean

But [as it's shown in the test class](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L27), when this bean is used in another bean, mock is not injected there (**it's relevant only for Kotlin**; there is a corrupted version of the bean, [even not nullable fields are null](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/main/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/Engine.kt#L4), [this](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/resources/mockito-extensions/org.Mockito.plugins.MockMaker) partially fixes it, instead of corrupted bean there is a normal instance (not a mock)).
what do you mean? Ok, if example with two empty classes and only Quarkus dependencies is "bad case" for you, I will try to find out Quarkus bug on my own.
My point is that the super simple Kotlin example I added above fails without running a Quarkus test, just a plain junit test

It doesn't fail, I send a screenshoot. Also I've pushed example without using Quarkus CDI in the same file, it works. 
Did you use master branch?
But making all classes as open resolves this issue, sorry, you are right.

Could you help with one more question? It still looks like there is an issue with Quarkus.

The problem with example above is final kotlin classes, as I said if I mark classes/method with I going to mock as open everything work, but in some cases I can't do it - e.g. when I want to use in CDI third-party class which is final and create it via `@Produces` API.

Mockito suggest using this [option](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/resources/mockito-extensions/org.Mockito.plugins.MockMaker#L1). When I add it example without Quarkus CDI [works correctly,](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L20) but [with Quarkus CDI it doesn't](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L36) (looks like there are two different instances (injected and test and injected in beans).
Isn't it a bug? Or just some unsupported feature. 

Are there other ways to deal with the case which I mentioned? When I want to mock final class and I can't mark it as open directly or via all-open plugin (third party api).

Thank you.

p.s. [This](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/resources/mockito-extensions/org.Mockito.plugins.MockMaker#L1) mockito option changes behaviour, without it quarkus can't mock final class and fails:

**Cannot mock/spy class test.quarkus.mocking.Engine
Mockito cannot mock/spy because :**
 **- final class**

With enabled option bean is mocked, but as it shown [there](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L36) mockito API doesn't, work (if I mark [mocked method](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/main/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/Engine.kt#L6) as open it works with quarkus too).

In order to be convinced that there is a Quarkus issue I'll need to see a very similar test that works as plain JUnit test and does not work when using `@QuarkusTest`.

At this point with all the things you mention I don't know what you expect me to test. So for me to look at this any more, I'll need to see (in your project) what I mentioned above.

So,

[This class](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L14) has both cases:
1. [Using Quarkus CDI](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L36), it doesn't work.
2. [Pure Junit](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L21), it works

I also created branch with Spring DI, [it works](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/spring/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L13) with the same setup (kotlin + final class + [enabled mockito feature to work with final classes](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/resources/mockito-extensions/org.Mockito.plugins.MockMaker#L1)).

Just to summarise:

- There is class `Car`
- There is class `Engine`
- `Engine` is injected in `Car`, `Engine.launch` just returns string, `ready` (**default**)
- `Engine` is created via [method api](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/main/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/BeanProducer.kt#L10) and it's final, in some cases it's impossible to mark class as open, e.g. - third party dependency. [This mockito feature](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/resources/mockito-extensions/org.Mockito.plugins.MockMaker#L1) allows mock even final classes.
- With [this](https://github.com/vadim-hleif/test-quarkus-mocking/blob/master/src/test/kotlin/test/quarkus/mocking/MockingTest.kt#L29) Quarkus API i can't mock `Engine.launch` result to `not ready`, because in the test and in `Car` I see different instances of `Engine`. Looks like `@InjectMock` doesn't work properly in such a case.

p.s. if try to mock not final class it works fine.
